title: CXCR5+ CD8 T Cells: Protective or Pathogenic?
summary: Review defining the CXCR5+ CD8 T cell as a distinct subset within the B cell follicle and germinal center under chronic antigen, phenotypically a non-exhausted effector-memory population functionally analogous to CD4 Tfh. CXCR5 and CD8 here are surface/protein markers (flow phenotype), consistent with the atlas Azimuth label being derived from transcript-level surrogates of the same subset.
quotes: Yet, a distinct CXCR5+ CD8 T cell subset identified within the B cell follicle and germinal center in situations of chronic antigen has recently been defined.
CD8 T cell localization to the B cell follicle suggests a functional profile similar to CD4 T follicular helper cells that are licensed to promote B cell responses.
CXCR5+ CD8 T cells control viral load during infection, and also promote antibody-mediated autoimmune disease progression.

title: CXCR5+CD8+ T cells are localized in B cell follicles and germinal centers and exhibit regulatory and anti-tumor function
summary: Identifies CD45RA-CXCR5+CD8+ T cells in human tonsillar tissue and follicular lymphoma by FACS and confocal microscopy, localised to germinal centers and T cell zones. Markers CXCR5, CD8, CD45RA are protein/surface (FACS + immunostaining). Functionally these cells suppress Tfh-driven B cell differentiation and produce higher IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha than CXCR5- CD8 cells.
quotes: We found that CXCR5+CD8+ T cells were present in high numbers and localized to GCs and T cell zones in the tonsillar tissues and FL, but present in low numbers in the peripheral blood.
Further analysis using intracellular cytokine staining showed that CXCR5+CD8+ T cells produced higher levels of IFN-γ and TNF-α compared to CXCR5-CD8+ subset.
These experiments indicated that CXCR5+CD8+ T cells suppressed Tfh function, as demonstrated by reduced differentiation of naive and/or memory B cells into plasmablasts cells (CD19intCD38+).

title: A Subset of CXCR5+CD8+ T Cells in the Germinal Centers From Human Tonsils and Lymph Nodes Help B Cells Produce Immunoglobulins
summary: Directly characterises a CXCR5+CD8+ T cell subset in germinal centers of human tonsils and lymph nodes, reporting a B-helper function (support of immunoglobulin production). Title-level evidence anchoring the tonsil/germinal-center localisation of this subset.
quotes: A Subset of CXCR5+CD8+ T Cells in the Germinal Centers From Human Tonsils and Lymph Nodes Help B Cells Produce Immunoglobulins

title: Follicular CD8+ T Cells: Origin, Function and Importance during HIV Infection
summary: Review of the phenotype, location, and origin of follicular CD8+ T cells. Establishes that this subset was first characterised infiltrating human tonsil follicles, is CD3+ CD4- (alpha-beta T cell), expresses high CXCR5 (protein) enabling entry to B cell zones, lacks CCR7, and migrates toward CXCL13. CXCR5/CCR7/CD8/CD4/CD3 stated as surface phenotype; note CXCR5 protein expression is what licenses follicular homing.
quotes: Quigley et al. first characterized a population of CD8 + T cells infiltrating human tonsil follicles and provided the insights into the phenotype and function of follicular CD8 + T cells (5).

Importantly, these cells express high levels of the C-X-C chemokine receptor type 5 (CXCR5), critical for entering the B cell zones in secondary lymphoid organs (13), and do not express the C-C chemokine receptor type 7 (CCR7), which directs them to the T cell zones (14).
In agreement with the expression of CXCR5, purified human CXCR5 + CD8 + T cells migrate in response to its ligand, the C-X-C motif ligand 13 (CXCL13) chemokine.

title: Follicular CD8 T cells accumulate in HIV infection and can kill infected cells in vitro via bispecific antibodies
summary: Examines human lymph nodes and tonsils and shows CD8 T cells infiltrate B cell follicles and germinal centers, with follicular CD8 (fCD8) cells retaining cytolytic potential (high granzyme B and perforin protein) despite reduced cytokine polyfunctionality. Establishes the follicle/GC localisation and cytolytic protein profile in human lymphoid tissue including tonsil.
quotes: Petrovas et al. examined human lymph nodes and tonsils and somewhat surprisingly found that CD8 T cells did infiltrate follicles in HIV-infected individuals.
Significantly increased frequencies of CD8 T cells in the B cell follicles and GCs were found in LNs from treated and untreated HIV-infected individuals.
Follicular CD8 (fCD8) T cells, despite compromised cytokine polyfunctionality, showed good cytolytic potential characterized by high ex vivo expression of granzyme B and perforin.

title: CXCR5+CD8+ T cells are a distinct functional subset with antitumor activity
summary: Defines CXCR5+CD8+ T cells as a distinct subset present in human tonsils and follicular lymphoma with strong cytotoxic activity, capable of suppressing Tfh-mediated B cell differentiation. RNA-seq (transcript-level) profiling revealed 77 differentially expressed genes unique to CXCR5+CD8+ T cells, of which a 33-gene upregulated signature correlated with survival — this is the transcriptomic counterpart to the surface CXCR5/CD8 phenotype.
quotes: We found that CXCR5+CD8+ T cells are present in human tonsils and follicular lymphoma, inhibit TFH-mediated B cell differentiation, and exhibit strong cytotoxic activity.
Furthermore, RNA-Seq-based transcriptional profiling revealed 77 differentially expressed genes unique to CXCR5+CD8+ T cells.

In summary, our study identified CXCR5+CD8+ T cells as a distinct T cell subset with ability to suppress TFH-mediated B cell differentiation, exert strong antitumor activity, and confer favorable prognosis in follicular lymphoma patients.

title: Cytolytic CD8+ T cells infiltrate germinal centers to limit ongoing HIV replication in spontaneous controller lymph nodes
summary: Spatial and transcriptional analysis of lymph-node follicular CD8 T cells (fCD8). Shows CXCR5+ fCD8s within germinal centers carry cytotoxic effector proteins (perforin, granzyme B) proximate to viral RNA foci, linking follicular localisation to cytolytic surveillance function. Perforin/granzyme B measured at protein level; transcriptional signatures of inflammatory chemotaxis and effector function also reported.
quotes: Follicular CD8+ T cells (fCD8) mediate surveillance in lymph node (LN) germinal centers against lymphotropic infections and cancers, but the precise mechanisms by which these cells mediate immune control remain incompletely resolved.
In HIV controllers, the cytotoxic effectors perforin and granzyme B were elevated among virus-specific CXCR5+ fCD8s proximate to foci of HIV RNA within germinal centers.

title: Cxc Chemokine Receptor 5 Expression Defines Follicular Homing T Cells with B Cell Helper Function
summary: Foundational study establishing CXCR5 (protein) as the marker of tonsillar follicular-homing T cells that migrate to CXCL13 (BCA-1) expressed in B cell follicles. Provides the mechanistic basis for CXCR5-driven follicular homing that defines the follicular CD8 subset.
quotes: Memory but not naive T cells from tonsils are CXCR5+ and migrate in response to the B cell–attracting chemokine 1 (BCA-1), which is selectively expressed by reticular cells and blood vessels within B cell follicles.
